itself, not a lifecycle state, not a promotion state, and not a reason to create
a new tree for every term. It names the threshold where a concept needs a
governed view because ordinary prose is no longer safe enough.

Candidate Definition reconstructed from an accepted normalization scaffold and exact CyberAlchemy-v2 source sections. It is not admitted and grants no implementation, migration, registry, publication, release, deployment, or external-effect authority.

Use view-bearing concept when a concept starts carrying enough work that future
agents need a dedicated lens over its meaning, system structure, run evidence,
residue, or promotion status. The view should make the concept inspectable and
usable without loading the whole repository.

In CyberAlchemy-lab migration work, Projection Specification is a prototype meaning reconstructed from CAL-NORMALIZE-01. It remains non-authoritative until the correct Lab owner admits a fully validated candidate.

Source context retained for reconstruction:

In CyberAlchemy v2, ontology is becoming a set of governed views over
knowledge. A view-bearing concept can support meaning views, architecture
views, run views, residue/challenge views, and promotion views. For
architecture specifically, architecture-pattern-inventory is the architecture
view interface that turns architecture evidence into reusable candidates before
CyberAlchemy authority decides promotion.
/home/vrondelli/projects/CyberAlchemy-lab

Some ideas become important enough to need their own dashboard, but the
dashboard still does not get to make the decision.

View-bearing concept is not a vault node type, not an ontology branch by
itself, not a lifecycle state, not a promotion state, and not a reason to create
a new tree for every term. It names the threshold where a concept needs a
governed view because ordinary prose is no longer safe enough.

For concept `c`, `view_bearing(c)` is admissible when:

```text
view_bearing(c) =
  distinct_evidence(c)
  and lifecycle_posture_needed(c)
  and owner_route(c)
  and reuse_surface(c)
  and challenge_or_drift_route(c)
```

The view attached to `c` must declare allowed readings and forbidden authority
moves. If those fields are absent, `c` remains a term, candidate, or local
concept rather than a view-bearing concept.

Projection Specification is the normalized definition identified by semantic.projection-specification, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D44 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A view-bearing concept is a load-bearing concept that needs its own governed
view or tree because it has distinct evidence, lifecycle posture, owner route,
reuse surface, and challenge/drift behavior that cannot be safely handled as
ordinary narrative vocabulary.

Not every term deserves a view. A concept may become view-bearing only when the
view helps preserve evidence, relations, lifecycle, owner route, reuse, or
challenge behavior without pretending to decide authority by itself.
Stable normalized identity for Projection Specification.

unresolved_notes: Exact normalized Projection Specification identity/type.definition/shared-authority scope versus primitive D44 View-Bearing Concept meaning needs an accepted role map.
Five-condition equality versus admissible-when/only-when wording and attached-view obligations remains a precedence interpretation.
Condition predicates are declarations, not proof of actual evidence distinctness, lifecycle need, owner routing, reuse or challenge behavior.
Load-bearing and ordinary-narrative-unsafe judgments have no accepted empirical threshold or operational test.
View-or-tree need does not require both structures, a particular file layout or creation of one tree per term.
Sorted evidence references do not prove actual evidence independence, completeness or preservation.
Lifecycle posture need is distinct from a lifecycle state and does not assign one.
A nonempty owner route is not live route resolution, approval or source-owner acceptance.
Reuse surface denotation and actual usability remain unaccepted.
One challenge-or-drift route does not require both mechanisms or an executed challenge event.
Explicit allowed-reading and forbidden-move sets may be empty; nonempty examples are required witnesses, not source-wide policy.
Absent declaration predicates denote missing candidate-record declarations, not epistemic unknown or absence of real historical fields.
Nominated and additional attached views are checked; reference aliases and actual view-universe completeness remain pending.
The six preservation roles form an inclusive disjunction; declared helpfulness does not establish actual preservation.
A five-condition record with absent required view fields is inconsistent with the combined declaration guards; no silent source rewrite or automatic fallback is used.
Canonical normalized Meaning records preserve declared accepted source relations without authenticating them or granting instance authority.
Independent actual authority is permitted; view fields, a dashboard, schema PASS or source admission cannot supply it alone.
Inspectability, usability and bounded repository context are declared design conditions rather than actual consumer evidence.
Context View, Ontology View and generated/projection carrier labels are separately qualified comparison meanings, not accepted aliases.
No whole upstream theory, accepted common-carrier map, shared consistency or semantic-cycle interpretation is imported.
Finite model checks and complete character accounting do not establish whole source fidelity or a universal/mechanized proof.
C53 admission overlay is separate from candidate-authored body, embedded candidate-unadmitted metadata, normalization scaffold and authority-effects ceiling.
